allow_large: The owner asked for this on 2026-10-02 (one explicit workers setting with three values, visible routing); six code files plus the tests and docs the contract change touches

amendments.because: The owner said on 2026-10-02 that Forge keeps no legacy: no one-time rewrite of codex to split
amendments.done_when: forge.toml's workers takes codex (every task and fix on Codex, user-facing included, using the design model's codex entry for user-facing work), claude (everything on Claude) or split (user-facing story tasks on Claude, the rest on Codex: today's behaviour). forge sync changes an existing workers = "codex" to "split" once, so an upgrade keeps behaviour and the file says it; new repos get split written explicitly. forge work prints one line before starting naming the worker, model and effort and why (for example 'Building PERMFLOW-1/T5 with Claude (claude-opus-5-5, high) because it is user-facing (workers = split)'), and forge next shows the worker beside each ready task. If the worker family changes between rounds of one item, the next forge work starts a fresh session on the new worker with the brief and the latest review findings. The skill and the AGENTS.md block explain the three values in one line each. Command-level tests cover each value for a user-facing task and a plain task, the sync rewrite, the printed line, and a family switch between rounds.

findings.body: With `workers = "claude"`, a user-facing item still enters the automatic Codex fallback when Claude is missing or fails without changing files. The fallback at `src/forge/worker.py:150–175` launches Codex despite the explicit Claude setting. This contradicts “everything on Claude” and means the owner cannot enforce the worker choice in forge.toml. Restrict fallback appropriately and cover the explicit Claude setting with a command-level failure test.
findings.title: Not done: forge.toml's workers takes codex, claude or split with explicit routing, visibility and fresh sessions

findings.body: `top` is the caller's checkout, but a ready task inherits forge.toml from its starting branch. `src/forge/task.py:143` selects the remote default branch or story branch, and lines 188 and 116 create the checkout from that base. For example, after changing PAGE's workers to Claude, running forge next from PAGE labels ready HELP as Claude even though HELP starts from a Codex-configured default branch. Resolve the configuration from the same base as task start. The new next test changes only the caller's uncommitted configuration, so it does not catch this mismatch.
findings.title: Not done: forge next names the worker that will actually build each ready task

findings.body: When the selected family has no Build/Fix/Lite model entry, this prints `(its own settings)` instead of the required model and effort. This occurs with an ordinary newly initialized repository after changing only workers to Claude: `src/forge/init.py:63–75` writes GPT-only entries, and `src/forge/repo.py:238` returns an empty selection for Claude. Resolve and report the effective model and effort, and test switching the initialized configuration through the real work command.
findings.title: Not done: the launch line names the model and effort when using worker defaults

findings.body: The switch guard applies only to the primary Codex launch. The fallback at `src/forge/worker.py:166–174` calls codex.conversation whenever `later` is true and can resume an older Codex conversation with the short prompt. After a Codex round, a successful split-mode Claude round, and then a clean Claude failure, the next round returns to that old Codex session instead of starting fresh with the whole brief and latest findings. Apply the family-switch check when choosing the fallback conversation and add a command-level regression for this sequence.
findings.title: Not done: a fallback family switch starts a fresh session with the whole brief

why: A story task marked user-facing always goes to a Claude worker even when forge.toml says workers = "codex", and nothing in forge.toml, forge next or forge work says so; the owner wants which agent builds what to be visible and switchable in one place
